patients.summary: Warehouse supervisor with type 2 diabetes who joins in 2020 and over six years develops CIDP (IVIG at neurology), an anal fistula (fistulotomy), nephrotic syndrome with a left renal vein thrombosis, tinea corporis, a recurrent L4-L5 radiculopathy and a left leg cellulitis. In May 2026 he is burned over 36% of his body in a house fire and is grafted at a burn center; last seen 2026-07-31.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
41 y/o man establishing care. Prior PCP office is consolidating; he wanted a smaller practice.

DM2: diagnosed around 2016. Metformin 1000 BID, takes it most days, admits the evening dose gets skipped when he works late. No hypoglycemia. Last A1c he remembers was 'around 7.' No known eye or kidney problems; last eye exam over a year ago.

Other hx: right-sided sciatica 2017 from a lumbar disc, MRI at the time showed a herniation per pt, did PT for 2 months and it went away. No back or leg symptoms now. Gets athlete's foot every so often, treats with drugstore creams. Perianal abscess drained at an urgent care in 2019, healed, no recurrence.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: father DM2, had kidney disease from it. Mother HTN. Sister has autoimmune thyroid disease.
Social: supervises a warehouse floor, on his feet most of the shift. Quit cigarettes in 2019. Beer socially, 1-2 a week. Lives in Easthampton.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as charted. Lungs clear. RRR, no murmur. Abd soft, nontender. Back: no tenderness, SLR negative bilaterally. Feet: skin intact, mild scaling between 4th-5th toes bilaterally, monofilament intact, DP pulses 2+.

A/P
1. DM2 - A1c, CMP, lipids, CBC, urine microalbumin today. Continue metformin. Eye exam referral to optometry.
2. Lipids - continue atorvastatin 20.
3. Hx lumbar disc herniation - quiescent.
4. Recurrent tinea pedis - currently minimal, OTC terbinafine cream if it flares.
5. HCM - Hep C screen today. Flu and Tdap given today. Requesting old records.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jason, your A1c came back at 7.1, which is right about where we want it. Cholesterol (LDL 92) is fine on the atorvastatin, kidney and liver tests normal, no protein in the urine, blood counts normal, hepatitis C screen negative. Keep doing what you're doing and try to catch that evening metformin. See you in March.

documents.title: Prior primary care records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records received by fax from patient's previous primary care office, 38 pages, covering 2014 to 2020. Includes problem list (type 2 diabetes since 2016, lumbar disc herniation 2017), medication list matching current, A1c values 6.8 to 7.4 since 2017, normal colorectal screening not yet due, normal annual labs, PT discharge summary from 2017 noting resolved right leg symptoms, urgent care note from 2019 for perianal abscess drainage. Indexed and routed to PCP. PCP reviewed: nothing new, consistent with history given.

documents.title: Refill request: metformin, atorvastatin
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy requested 90-day supplies of metformin 1000 mg BID and atorvastatin 20 mg daily for mail order. Last visit 9/14, A1c 7.1. Sent per protocol, 90 days with 1 refill.

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here before his shift. Feels fine. Using a pill box now, says he misses maybe one dose a week. Walking the warehouse floor counts as exercise, he says. Eye appointment still not made - gave him the optometry number again.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 20.
O: vitals as charted. Feet: no lesions, sensation intact. Toe webs clear today.
A/P: DM2, stable. A1c and BMP today. Keep current regimen. COVID vaccine - eligible soon through his employer group, encouraged. Physical in September.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 7.0 - slightly better than September. Kidney function and potassium normal. Nice work with the pill box.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
42 y/o M, annual.
Interval: no illnesses. Two COVID shots in April. Still hasn't seen optometry; says he'll go this month.
ROS: negative except occasional low back stiffness after long shifts, no leg symptoms.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 20. NKDA.
Social: unchanged; no tobacco since 2019.
PHQ-2: 0.

Exam: Vitals as charted. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyroid enlargement. Lungs clear. Heart regular, no murmurs. Abdomen soft. Skin: no rashes. Extremities without swelling. Neuro: strength 5/5 throughout, reflexes 2+ and symmetric. Diabetic foot exam: intact skin, monofilament normal, pulses present.

A/P:
- DM2: A1c, CMP, lipids, CBC, urine microalbumin.
- Vaccines: flu and PCV20 given (diabetes indication). Booster when eligible.
- Colon screening at 45.
RTC 6 mo.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP

documents.body: Outside optometry practice, date of exam 10/12/2021. Dilated fundus exam both eyes: no diabetic retinopathy, no macular edema. Visual acuity 20/20 OD, 20/25 OS with correction. Recommend annual dilated exam.

orders.reason: progressive symmetric weakness with reduced reflexes

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit: weakness
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: weak arms and legs.

HPI: Since sometime in November (he isn't sure of the week) he's noticed his legs giving out on the stairs at work and he has trouble getting boxes up onto the top racks. Gradual, worse over 3 months. Some pins-and-needles in fingers and soles, comes and goes. No back pain, no bowel or bladder change, no double vision or trouble swallowing, no recent illness or diarrhea before it started. No new meds.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, speech normal, cranial nerves intact. Strength 4/5 hip flexors and shoulder abductors both sides, 4+/5 grip and ankle dorsiflexion both sides. Reflexes 1+ biceps, trace patellar, absent ankles - symmetric. Sensation to pinprick a bit reduced in fingertips and toes. Gait slow but steady, can't rise from a squat without using his hands.

A/P: Symmetric proximal and distal weakness with hyporeflexia over ~3 months in a diabetic - this is more than diabetic neuropathy. Checking CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, CK, A1c. Neurology referral, asked for an early slot. Told him to go to the ED for any trouble breathing, swallowing or rapid worsening. Light duty note for work.

documents.title: Neurology appointment?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hey doc, haven't heard from neurology yet. Is there anything I should do in the meantime? Stairs are the same, not worse.

documents.title: RE: Neurology appointment?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jason - the referral went out Tuesday and our referral coordinator is calling them today to push for something sooner. Your labs came back normal: thyroid, B12, muscle enzyme (CK), kidney and liver tests and blood counts. A1c 7.4. Normal labs are useful, they rule out several common causes. Same precautions as we talked about - any trouble breathing or swallowing, go straight to the ED.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth three times daily

reports.text: Motor and sensory nerve conduction studies of the upper and lower limbs bilaterally with needle EMG of selected muscles. Motor conduction velocities are slowed in the median, ulnar, peroneal and tibial nerves bilaterally, with prolonged distal motor latencies. Sensory responses are reduced in amplitude in the hands and feet. Needle EMG: no spontaneous activity; reduced recruitment in distal muscles.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology group. Date of visit 05/16/2022. Referred by primary care.

Reason for consult: weakness of all four limbs.

Mr. Kane is a 42-year-old warehouse supervisor with type 2 diabetes on metformin who describes roughly half a year of steadily increasing weakness in both arms and both legs. Stairs have become hard and he cannot lift stock above shoulder height. Intermittent tingling of the hands and feet.

PMH: type 2 diabetes; prior lumbar disc herniation 2017; remote perianal abscess drainage. Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily. Allergies: none known. Family history: father type 2 diabetes with kidney disease, mother hypertension, sister autoimmune thyroid disease. Former smoker, quit 2019; occasional alcohol.

Examination: weakness in both proximal and distal muscle groups of all four limbs, symmetric. Reflexes diminished throughout. Mild loss of sensation in a glove-and-stocking pattern. Cranial nerves normal.

Studies: Nerve conduction studies 05/05/2022 with slowed conduction velocities and prolonged distal latencies (report enclosed). Lumbar puncture 05/09/2022: CSF protein elevated, cell count normal.

Impression: chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy.

Plan:
1. IVIG induction, 2 g/kg divided over 5 days, then maintenance 1 g/kg every 3 weeks; we are obtaining insurance authorization and will schedule at our infusion center.
2. Gabapentin 300 mg three times daily for the paresthesias.
3. Physical therapy for strengthening.
4. Follow-up in 3 to 4 months.

Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Neurology letter review
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt after PCP reviewed neurology letter. He has started gabapentin 300 TID, a little drowsy on day one, better now. Neurology's office is working on authorization for IVIG; he has not heard a start date. Med list updated. Follow-up with PCP booked mid June.

medications.drug_text: 100 ML immunoglobulin G, human 100 MG/ML Injection
medications.sig: 1 g/kg IV every 3 weeks at neurology infusion center (interval per neurology)

documents.title: Follow-up: CIDP
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Neurology letter reviewed with him - CIDP. Five days of IVIG loading finished 6/6 through 6/10 at the neurology infusion suite, mild headache day 2, nothing else. Next dose late June, then every 3 weeks. Too early to tell if stronger. Gabapentin helping the tingling at night. Started PT twice a week.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 20, gabapentin 300 TID, IVIG per neurology.
O: vitals as charted. Proximal strength 4/5 legs, unchanged. Feet intact.
A/P:
- CIDP: on IVIG per neurology. Med list updated.
- DM2: A1c 7.4 in Feb; recheck at physical.
- Work: extended light duty note through August.

documents.title: Office Visit: perianal pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Embarrassed to bring it up. For about six months, on and off, pain near the anus that's worse when he has a BM, and a smelly discharge that stains his underwear. Near where the abscess was drained in 2019. No fever, no rectal bleeding, no diarrhea or weight loss.
O: afebrile. Perianal skin: small opening just beside the anal verge with mild redness and tenderness around it, a bit of discharge on the gauze. No fluctuance.
A/P: Probable anal fistula after the old abscess. Referral to general surgery. Sitz baths, keep area clean and dry. Call if fever or a painful swelling develops.

documents.title: General surgery consultation
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Outside general surgery group. Date of service 07/21/2022. Referred by primary care for perianal symptoms.

History: 42-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and CIDP diagnosed this spring, now on IVIG. Six months of intermittent pain around the anus, worse with bowel movements, and persistent malodorous drainage. Perianal abscess drained in 2019.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, gabapentin 300 mg TID, IVIG every 3 weeks. Allergies: none known.

Exam: Perianal erythema and tenderness. A small external opening is present adjacent to the anal verge. Digital rectal exam is painful and there is induration in the perianal tissue; no mass felt in the rectum, prostate unremarkable.

Labs this morning: WBC 9.0, hemoglobin 13.5, fasting glucose 160, CRP 2.8 mg/L.

Assessment: anorectal fistula, likely from the prior abscess.

Plan: exam under anesthesia with fistulotomy as a day surgery case; scheduled 08/11. Pre-op instructions given. Hold metformin the morning of surgery.

documents.title: Operative report: EUA and fistulotomy
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Outside ambulatory surgery center. Date of surgery 08/11/2022.
Preoperative and postoperative diagnosis: anorectal fistula.
Procedure: examination under anesthesia, fistulotomy.
Anesthesia: general with local infiltration. Position: prone jackknife.
Findings: external opening beside the anal verge; a single tract probed to an internal opening at the dentate line, involving only a small portion of the sphincter. No other openings, no abscess cavity. Anoscopy otherwise normal.
Procedure: tract opened over the probe, granulation tissue curetted, edges marsupialized. Hemostasis with cautery. Dressing applied.
EBL minimal. No complications. Discharged home the same day with sitz baths, stool softener and acetaminophen. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

documents.title: General surgery follow-up
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body: Outside general surgery group, 09/08/2022. Four weeks after fistulotomy. No pain, drainage stopped about 10 days after surgery, continent. Wound fully epithelialized, no residual opening, no induration. Fistula healed. Discharged from our care; return if symptoms recur.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body: Outside neurology group, 09/12/2022. CIDP on maintenance IVIG 1 g/kg every 3 weeks since June induction. He reports he can take stairs at work again and is lifting to shoulder height; overhead still hard by the end of a shift. Tingling improved on gabapentin. Exam: strength improved to 4+/5 proximally and 5-/5 distally; reflexes remain diminished; sensory exam stable. Plan: continue IVIG every 3 weeks and gabapentin; continue home exercise program; return in 6 to 9 months.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
43 y/o M. Busy year: CIDP diagnosed in May, on IVIG q3wk, clearly stronger - walked in without the railing today. Fistulotomy in August, healed per surgery. Back at full duty since Labor Day.
ROS: tingling feet at night improved. No chest pain, dyspnea, swelling. Bowel habits normal.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 20, gabapentin 300 TID, IVIG q3wk (neurology). NKDA.
PHQ-9: 3 - says the spring was stressful, fine now.
Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear, heart regular. Abdomen benign. Legs without edema. Strength 4+/5 hip flexors, reflexes reduced (known). Feet: monofilament diminished at toes (CIDP), skin intact, pulses good.
A/P: DM2 - labs today. CIDP - per neurology. Flu and bivalent COVID today. Eye exam due next month. Colon screening discussion at 45.

documents.title: Results from your physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your A1c is 7.2. Cholesterol, kidney, liver and blood counts all look fine. No changes needed.

documents.title: Diabetic eye exam report
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Optometry exam 10/06/2022. Dilated exam OU: no diabetic retinopathy. Mild refractive change, new glasses prescribed. Return 1 year.

orders.reason: edema with heavy proteinuria and low albumin

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit: leg swelling
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Over the last few weeks both legs have been swelling, socks leave deep marks, boots tight by noon. Scale says he's up about 11 lb and he hasn't been eating more. Some dull discomfort in the left flank, no burning with urination, no blood he's noticed, urine maybe foamy. No chest pain or shortness of breath, sleeps flat. Last IVIG 10/18.
O: weight 99 kg (94 at the physical a month ago). BP and HR as charted. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, nontender, no CVA tenderness on the right, mild discomfort to deep palpation in the left flank. 2+ pitting edema to mid-shin both sides.
UA dip in office: protein 3+.
A/P: New edema with heavy proteinuria in a diabetic - concern for nephrotic syndrome. CMP sent. Urgent nephrology referral. Leg elevation, low salt. Will call with labs.

documents.title: Lab results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt. Albumin 2.5 (low), creatinine 0.9 (kidney filtration fine). With the urine protein this looks like nephrotic syndrome. Our coordinator got him a nephrology new-patient slot 11/14; asked them to put him on the cancellation list. Reviewed: ED for shortness of breath, chest pain, or sudden leg pain/swelling on one side. He understands.

documents.title: Nephrology consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology practice. Date of visit 11/14/2022. Referred by primary care.

HPI: 43-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, CIDP on IVIG and a recent fistulotomy, sent for swelling of both legs that has been building over several weeks with unintended weight gain. Also describes discomfort in the left flank.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, gabapentin 300 mg TID, IVIG every 3 weeks. He takes no anticoagulant or antiplatelet agent. Allergies: none known.

Family history: father with diabetic kidney disease. Former smoker (quit 2019).

Exam: vital signs stable. Pitting edema of both lower extremities. Abdomen soft and nontender. On standing there is palpable fullness above the left testis.

Data: urinalysis with marked proteinuria. Urine protein/creatinine ratio 6.8 g/g. Serum albumin 2.4. Creatinine 0.9, filtration preserved.

Assessment: nephrotic syndrome with preserved kidney function. The left flank discomfort and left-sided scrotal fullness raise concern for left renal vein involvement.

Plan:
1. Lisinopril 10 mg daily for proteinuria.
2. Furosemide 40 mg daily for edema; 2 g sodium diet.
3. CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast, venous phase, this week.
4. BMP in 2 to 3 weeks through primary care.
5. Return in 3 months, sooner pending imaging.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Indication: nephrotic syndrome, left flank pain. Technique: CT of the abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast including a delayed venous phase. Findings: Filling defect expanding the left renal vein from the renal hilum toward the inferior vena cava, consistent with thrombus. IVC patent. Kidneys normal in size with symmetric enhancement; no hydronephrosis, no renal mass. Liver, spleen, pancreas and adrenals unremarkable. No lymphadenopathy. Small amount of subcutaneous edema. Bowel and bladder unremarkable. No free fluid.

conditions.label: Embolism and thrombosis of renal vein

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets by mouth twice daily for 7 days, then 1 tablet twice daily

documents.title: Nephrology addendum
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body: Outside nephrology practice, addendum 11/21/2022. CT 11/18 shows left renal vein thrombosis, IVC clear. Spoke with the patient by phone today. Starting apixaban 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily, planned for about 12 months while nephrotic and pending repeat imaging. Bleeding precautions reviewed. Prescription sent. Copy to primary care.

documents.title: Medication reconciliation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt after nephrology letters came in. Taking lisinopril 10, furosemide 40 (peeing a lot, legs a little better), started apixaban last night - knows the 2-pills-twice-a-day week then 1 twice a day. No NSAIDs; acetaminophen for aches. Told him to let neurology's infusion team know he is on a blood thinner. BMP at nurse visit 12/6. List updated.

documents.title: Nurse visit: BMP and weight
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for labs ordered after nephrology started lisinopril and furosemide. Weight 96 kg, down 3 kg from 10/27. Swelling better, ankles still puffy by evening. No dizziness on standing. Apixaban without bleeding. BP as charted. BMP drawn. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: BMP result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Potassium and kidney function are normal on the new medicines. I sent a copy to nephrology. Keep the salt down and keep going.
